summary: Step-by-step guide to bringing SDI video from an AJA card into a level with a Media Bundle (keying, lens undistortion via its Material Instance) and sending camera views out to the card via the Media Capture window in editor or a Create Media Capture Blueprint at runtime.
gotchas: Store the Media Capture in a variable or garbage collection may destroy it
Capture only works in New Editor Window (PIE) or Standalone Game, not Selected Viewport or Simulate
Viewport resolution must match the output resolution in the active Media Profile

summary: Reference of every Configuration dropdown and Details panel setting on Blackmagic Media Source and Blackmagic Media Output assets (device, resolution, color format, deinterlacing, OCIO, timecode, sync, fill/key, HDR, buffers).
gotchas: Tested only on DeckLink 4K Extreme 12G, DeckLink Duo 2, DeckLink 8K Pro
Fill and Key not available with 10bit RGB 4:4:4; that format needs width divisible by 64
Framelock does not function for Blackmagic sources
Do not enable Wait for Sync Event if already genlocked with a custom time step

summary: Step-by-step guide to playing SDI input from a Blackmagic card in a level via a Media Bundle and sending camera views out to the card using the Media Capture window or a runtime Blueprint toggle.
gotchas: Store the Media Capture in a variable or garbage collection may destroy it
Capture only works in New Editor Window (PIE) or Standalone Game, not Selected Viewport or Simulate
Viewport resolution must match the output resolution in the active Media Profile

summary: Reference of settings on NDI Media Source and NDI Media Output assets, noting which shared capture-card fields are nonfunctional for NDI (bandwidth, timecode sync, source/group name, audio, Wait for Sync Event).
keys: Send Audio Only if Receivers Connected
gotchas: Do not disable the Auto checkbox in the source Configuration dropdown
Most Media Connection/Media Mode fields are nonfunctional for NDI
Wait for Sync Event behaves differently from the AJA/Blackmagic setting of the same name

summary: Quick start for receiving an NDI stream onto a Media Plate actor and sending camera views out as an NDI stream via the Media Capture window or a runtime Blueprint toggle.
gotchas: Requires NDI Tools installed and an NDI source streaming
Store the Media Capture in a variable or garbage collection may destroy it
Capture only works in PIE New Editor Window or Standalone Game; viewport resolution must match Media Profile output

summary: Explains Media Profiles and Proxy Media Source/Output assets for switching a project's video inputs, outputs, timecode and genlock setup in one click, with a walkthrough of file-based vs live SDI profiles.
gotchas: Only one Media Profile can be active at a time
Active profile choice is saved per computer in editor; packaged builds use Startup Media Profile
Capture stops if the switched-to profile has no output at that index

summary: How to make the engine adopt timecode from an AJA or Blackmagic SDI input and genlock its frame rate to it using TimecodeProvider and Custom TimeStep Blueprint classes, plus how to view timecode and decode timecode texel encoding.
gotchas: Timecode and genlock management is under active development and likely to change
Restart the editor after setting TimecodeProvider/Custom TimeStep in Project Settings

summary: Tour of the Virtual Studio sample: its AJA/Blackmagic/File Media Profiles, Media Bundles fed through proxies, chroma keying, CameraSwitcher UMG capture controls, a looping video wall, and the modular studio asset kit.
gotchas: Capturing output requires a supported AJA or Blackmagic SDI card
FileMediaProfile has no outputs configured
Capture only works in PIE New Editor Window or Standalone Game

summary: Short steps to enable nDisplay in an existing project: enable the plugin and project setting, restart, then import a .cfg/.ndisplay file or create an nDisplay Config asset.
gotchas: Restart the editor after enabling

summary: Explains how nDisplay renders inner-frustum motion blur while subtracting tracked camera motion, for LED-wall process shots, comparing Move the Stage vs Move the World setups.
gotchas: Move the Stage accuracy not fully validated; Move the World considered reliable
Large translations far from origin can make rendering unstable
A panning physical camera always blurs the wall

summary: Lists nDisplay cluster Network timeout settings and the four default TCP ports (41001-41004), and where to change sync, cluster event and Switchboard ports.
gotchas: Ports 41001-41004 must be open on all computers
Switchboard and SwitchboardListener must use the same port

summary: Explains applying color grading (additive stack) and OpenColorIO (non-additive overrides) to the whole nDisplay cluster, per viewport, or to the inner frustum per node.
gotchas: Root Actor changes are per-instance and not saved to the Config UAsset
Per-viewport color grading does not affect the inner frustum
If a viewport/node is in multiple OCIO overrides, only the last listed applies

summary: Guidelines for authoring UV1 on nDisplay LED stage projection meshes (uniform texel density, no overlap, layout matching the physical wall) so ICVFX UV Light Cards and Chroma Key markers work.
gotchas: UV channel 0 is reserved for mesh-policy warp mapping
Keep meshes separate; do not combine on export
Flipped UV shells make controls feel backward

summary: Overview of nDisplay multi-process rendering, which runs an onscreen and a headless offscreen engine process per node on separate GPUs, versus multi-GPU, with hardware prerequisites.
gotchas: Needs at least two GPUs with SLI disabled (no Premium Mosaic)
Disabling Hyper-Threading/SMT recommended
Recommended for NVIDIA Ada Lovelace GPUs which lack NVLink

summary: How to replicate actor transform changes from the nDisplay primary node to cluster nodes with sync components, and custom data via IDisplayClusterClusterSyncObject.
gotchas: Only transforms are synced, not full replication
All input is handled only by the primary node

summary: Reference for the legacy text nDisplay config file (.cfg/.ndisplay) sections and parameters: cluster_node, window, viewport, projection, screen, postprocess, camera, scene_node, input, input_setup, general, nvidia, network, info, custom.
gotchas: Imported .cfg/.ndisplay files convert to .uasset; exported .ndisplay lacks tracking features
addr must be IPv4; IPv6 not supported
MPCDI support limited to version 1.0 with 2D and A3D profiles
Do not set info version by hand

summary: Explains nDisplay viewport overscan (render extra pixels then crop) to keep post effects continuous across cluster nodes, with a table of which rendering, gameplay and media features are compatible.
gotchas: Auto-exposure must stay disabled; overscan cannot fix it
Only works when the post effect range stays within the overscan percentage
Lens flare, DoF, SSR, SSGI should be avoided
Niagara emitters need Deterministic enabled; Blueprints need seeded randoms

summary: Explains nDisplay cluster architecture (primary and secondary nodes), the config-asset workflow, failover, multi-GPU viewport rendering, the DisplayCluster Blueprint API, C++ extension points, and OS support.
gotchas: Externally specified config (Switchboard/command line) overrides a config actor in the level
Failover only handles network-discoverable render node failures
Linux support is preliminary; ray tracing not supported there

summary: How to use the nDisplay Launch plugin's toolbar button to launch nDisplay nodes locally for testing, plus its options and project settings (Multi-User, Unreal Insights, console variable presets, command-line args).
gotchas: Requires nDisplay and nDisplay Launch plugins plus a config with a working cluster node
Do not prefix command-line args with a dash
Without MaxGPUCount=2 a second GPU is not used

summary: First-run guide: create a project from the nDisplay template, preview the NDC_Basic config, and launch a cluster node with Switchboard and SwitchboardListener.
gotchas: nDisplay does not run in the editor; it launches as a separate -game instance
Do not mix loopback 127.0.0.1 with non-loopback addresses in multi-machine setups
Cooked builds need the .exe path set and UProject path emptied in Switchboard

summary: Reference for nDisplay Root Actor and ICVFX Camera Component Details settings: viewport screen percentage, overscan, hidden content, color grading, OCIO, light cards, editor preview, inner frustum, camera motion blur, chromakey, texture replacement.
gotchas: nDisplay color grading/OCIO only affects nDisplay renders, not editor or Movie Render Queue
Disabling Enable Inner Frustum on the root disables it for all ICVFX cameras

summary: How to configure each nDisplay viewport projection policy in the 3D Config Editor: Simple, Camera, Manual, Mesh, MPCDI (native or explicit PFM), EasyBlend, VIOSO, and DomeProjection.
gotchas: Mesh policy uses UV channel 0 for warp mapping
Calibration must be done in the vendor tool first for EasyBlend/VIOSO/DomeProjection

summary: How to set up stereo output in nDisplay (interpupillary distance, swap eyes, Side-by-Side/Top-bottom render mode in Switchboard) or produce stereo pairs from two monoscopic View Origins with Stereo Offset.
gotchas: Frame sequential usually needs a GPU with specialized stereo support
You must configure GPU/driver/hardware to route the stereo images

summary: Explains software and hardware sync for nDisplay clusters (determinism, genlock vs framelock, daisy chain, Mosaic/EyeFinity) and the Render Sync Policy options, with the NVIDIA swap-lock setup workflow.
gotchas: Hardware sync needs NVIDIA Quadro cards, Sync II cards and a genlock generator
Sync group/barrier value 0 is not allowed
Thread barriers cannot be disabled
Mosaic spanning multiple GPUs in one PC is slow and not recommended

summary: How to show 2D calibration test patterns across nDisplay viewports with the Display Cluster Test Patterns Actor via console command or cluster event, with the parameters for each built-in pattern.
gotchas: An unmatched pattern ID removes the current test pattern
Custom patterns must be Post-Process Materials added to Calibration Patterns
